# Course Syllabus

## Building Connected Systems: API-First Software Architecture
**Course Code:** CS 3350  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** CS 2350 (Object-Oriented Programming), CS 2400 (Data Structures)  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  

---

## Course Description

This foundational course explores software development through the lens of API-first design principles, teaching students to architect and build interconnected systems from the ground up. Students learn to design, implement, and consume RESTful and GraphQL APIs while understanding how modern applications communicate across distributed environments. The course emphasizes hands-on development of microservices, third-party API integration, and real-world connectivity patterns. Through progressive projects, students build a complete ecosystem of communicating services, from simple data endpoints to complex authentication systems. Topics include API specification languages (OpenAPI/Swagger), versioning strategies, error handling, rate limiting, and security considerations. Students gain practical experience with popular frameworks, testing methodologies for API endpoints, and documentation practices that enable effective team collaboration. The curriculum balances theoretical concepts with industry-standard tools and practices, preparing students to contribute immediately to modern software teams. By course completion, students understand how APIs serve as the backbone of contemporary software architecture and can confidently design systems that scale across web, mobile, and IoT platforms while maintaining security and performance standards.

---

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and implement RESTful and GraphQL APIs** using industry-standard frameworks and specification languages
• **Architect connected systems** using API-first principles and microservices patterns for scalable software solutions  
• **Integrate third-party services** and develop secure authentication mechanisms for distributed application ecosystems

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundation and Testing Principles
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD): Building Reliable Software Through Testing First
- Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The core TDD workflow of writing a failing test (Red), implementing minimal code to pass (Green), and improving the design (Refactor)
- Unit Testing: Writing isolated tests that verify individual functions or methods work correctly, forming the foundation of the TDD approach
- **Activity:** Code Quality Assessment: Evaluating Three Password Validation Functions (60 min)

### Week 2: API Fundamentals and REST Principles
- Introduction to API-first architecture
- REST architectural constraints and principles
- HTTP methods, status codes, and headers
- **Activity:** Code Review Evaluation: Comparing Two JavaScript Function Implementations (65 min)

### Week 3: Designing RESTful APIs
- Resource identification and URI design
- JSON data formats and content negotiation
- API specification with OpenAPI/Swagger
- **Lab Report Due:** Basic Web Calculator Lab Report (100 points)

### Week 4: Building Your First API
- Setting up development environment (Node.js/Express or Python/FastAPI)
- Implementing CRUD operations
- Request validation and error handling

### Week 5: Advanced REST Concepts
- Nested resources and relationships
- Pagination, filtering, and sorting
- **Activity:** Code Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Tracker Application Implementations (100 min)

### Week 6: API Testing and Documentation
- Writing comprehensive API tests
- Integration testing strategies
- Interactive API documentation
- **Quiz:** Software Development Fundamentals Quiz (100 points)

### Week 7: Authentication and Security
- JWT tokens and session management
- OAuth 2.0 and third-party authentication
- API security best practices
- **Activity:** Code Review Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Fix Solutions (85 min)

### Week 8: GraphQL Introduction
- GraphQL vs REST comparison
- Schema definition and resolvers
- Queries, mutations, and subscriptions

### Week 9: Building GraphQL APIs
- GraphQL server implementation
- Schema design patterns
- Performance optimization techniques
- **Activity:** Code Quality Evaluation: Comparing Two Basic Calculator Implementations (85 min)

### Week 10: Microservices Architecture
- Microservices patterns and principles
- Service communication strategies
- **Activity:** Code Review Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Fixes and Code Improvements (45 min)

### Week 11: Third-Party API Integration
- Consuming external APIs
- Rate limiting and error handling
- API key management and security

### Week 12: API Versioning and Evolution
- Versioning strategies (URL, header, content negotiation)
- Backward compatibility considerations
- **Activity:** Code Quality Assessment: Evaluating Password Validation Functions (55 min)

### Week 13: Performance and Scalability
- Caching strategies (Redis, CDN)
- Load balancing and horizontal scaling
- Monitoring and logging

### Week 14: Production Deployment
- CI/CD pipelines for APIs
- Container orchestration basics
- **Portfolio Due:** Personal Portfolio Website Development Project (100 points)

### Week 15: Real-World Case Studies and Review
- Industry API examples and analysis
- Course review and exam preparation
- **Presentation:** Personal Software Project Showcase Presentation (100 points)

### Week 16: Final Exam Week
- **Final Exam:** Personal Task Manager Application - Programming Fundamentals Exam (100 points)

# COMP 3850: Test-Driven Software Architecture
## Building Bulletproof Applications from the Ground Up

#### Course Description

This intensive, project-driven course revolutionizes how students approach software development by placing testing at the absolute center of the development process. Students will master the art of writing tests before code, designing software architectures that are inherently testable, and implementing comprehensive testing strategies across multiple layers of complex applications. Through hands-on development of three major projects—a distributed microservices system, a real-time collaborative application, and a data-intensive analytics platform—students will experience the full spectrum of testing challenges in modern software development. The course emphasizes practical mastery of advanced testing frameworks, continuous integration pipelines, mutation testing, property-based testing, and performance testing under realistic load conditions. Students will work in rotating teams, conducting rigorous code reviews focused on testability and test coverage. By semester's end, students will have internalized a test-first mindset and possess the technical skills to architect, build, and maintain enterprise-grade software systems with confidence. This course bridges the gap between academic computer science and professional software development practices.

### Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and implement comprehensive test suites** using TDD/BDD methodologies for complex, multi-tier software architectures
• **Architect software systems with testability** as a primary design constraint, demonstrating mastery of dependency injection, mocking, and modular design patterns  
• **Deploy and maintain automated testing pipelines** integrating unit, integration, end-to-end, and performance testing in CI/CD environments

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: TDD Fundamentals and JavaScript Testing
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) with JavaScript
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The core TDD workflow of writing failing tests (Red), implementing minimal code to pass (Green), and improving code structure (Refactor)
  - Unit Testing: Writing isolated tests that verify individual functions or components work correctly with specific inputs and expected outputs
- **Activities:** Code Quality Detective: Evaluating Bug-Prone vs. Clean Code Samples (55 min)
- 
### Week 2: Unit Testing Frameworks Deep Dive
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) with Unit Testing Frameworks
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The three-phase TDD process of writing failing tests (Red), implementing minimal passing code (Green), and improving code structure (Refactor)
  - Unit Testing: Testing individual components or functions in isolation to verify they behave as expected with various inputs and edge cases
- **Activities:** Code Review Battle: Evaluating Bug-Prone vs Clean Code Solutions (50 min)
- 
### Week 3: Test Coverage and Measurement
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) with JavaScript and Jest
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The three-phase TDD process of writing failing tests (Red), making tests pass (Green), and improving code structure (Refactor)
  - Test Coverage: Measurement of how much source code is executed during testing, including line, branch, and function coverage metrics
- **Activities:** Code Review Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Fixes in Simple Python Functions (55 min)
- - **Assessment:** Software Development Fundamentals Quiz (100 points)

### Week 4: Advanced TDD Implementation
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) Implementation and Best Practices
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The core TDD workflow of writing failing tests, implementing passing code, then improving design
  - Unit Testing: Creating isolated tests that verify individual components or functions work correctly in isolation
- **Activities:** Code Review Evaluation: Assessing Bug Fixes in a Simple Calculator Program (50 min)
- 
### Week 5: TDD with Complex Systems
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) Implementation
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The three-phase TDD process of writing failing tests, implementing minimal code to pass, then improving code structure
  - Unit Testing: Isolated testing of individual components or functions to verify correct behavior independent of external dependencies
- **Activities:** Code Review Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Fixes and Best Practices (65 min)
- 
### Week 6: Testing Frameworks Mastery
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) Fundamentals
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The three-phase TDD process of writing failing tests, implementing minimal code, and improving design
  - Unit Testing Frameworks: Tools like JUnit, pytest, or Mocha that provide structure and assertions for automated testing
- **Activities:** Code Quality Assessment: Evaluating HTML/CSS Web Page Implementations (60 min)
- - **Assessment:** Introduction to Programming Languages and Development Tools Discussion (100 points)

### Week 7: API Testing and RESTful Services
**Module:** API Design and RESTful Web Services
- **Concepts:**
  - REST (Representational State Transfer): Architectural style for distributed systems emphasizing stateless communication and resource-based URLs
  - HTTP Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH operations that define actions performed on API resources
- **Activities:** Code Review Battle: Evaluating Bug-Fix Solutions (65 min)
- 
### Week 8: **PROJECT 1 WEEK - Distributed Microservices System**
- **Focus:** Apply TDD principles to build a distributed microservices system
- **Activities:** Code Review Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Fixes in HTML/CSS Projects (55 min)
- - **Assessment:** Personal Portfolio Website Development Project (100 points)

### Week 9: Integration Testing and Test Doubles
**Module:** Advanced Testing Patterns
- **Concepts:**
  - Integration Testing: Testing interactions between multiple components or systems
  - Test Doubles: Mocks, stubs, fakes, and spies for isolating units under test
- **Activities:** Code Review Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Fixes in a Simple Calculator Program (50 min)
- 
### Week 10: Behavior-Driven Development (BDD)
**Module:** BDD and Specification by Example
- **Concepts:**
  - BDD Framework: Using natural language specifications to drive development
  - Acceptance Testing: Verifying system behavior from user perspective
- **Activities:** Code Review Evaluation: Assessing Bug Fix Quality and Implementation Approaches (45 min)
- 
### Week 11: **PROJECT 2 WEEK - Real-time Collaborative Application**
- **Focus:** Implement BDD practices for real-time systems
- - **Assessment:** Personal Portfolio Website Development Exam (100 points)

### Week 12: Performance Testing and Load Testing
**Module:** Non-Functional Testing
- **Concepts:**
  - Performance Testing: Measuring system responsiveness and stability under load
  - Load Testing: Simulating realistic user loads to identify bottlenecks
- 
### Week 13: CI/CD Pipeline Integration
**Module:** Automated Testing in DevOps
- **Concepts:**
  - Continuous Integration: Automated testing on code changes
  - Deployment Pipeline: Automated testing stages from unit to production
- 
### Week 14: **PROJECT 3 WEEK - Data-Intensive Analytics Platform**
- **Focus:** Testing data processing, ETL pipelines, and analytics
- 
### Week 15: Advanced Testing Topics
**Module:** Mutation Testing and Property-Based Testing
- **Concepts:**
  - Mutation Testing: Evaluating test quality by introducing code changes
  - Property-Based Testing: Generating test cases based on system properties
- - **Assessment:** My First Programming Project - Interactive Calculator Presentation (100 points)

### Week 16: **FINAL PROJECT PRESENTATIONS**
- Student presentations of major projects
- Peer code reviews and testing strategy evaluations
- Course wrap-up and industry best practices discussion

---

## Assessment Plan

|------------|------|--------|----------|---------|
| Software Development Fundamentals Quiz | Quiz | 100 | Week 3 | 10% |
| Programming Languages Discussion | Discussion | 100 | Week 6 | 10% |
| Portfolio Website Development | Portfolio | 100 | Week 8 | 15% |
| Portfolio Website Development Exam | Exam | 100 | Week 11 | 15% |
| Calculator Project Presentation | Presentation | 100 | Week 15 | 10% |
| **Major Project 1:** Microservices System | Project | 200 | Week 8 | 15% |
| **Major Project 2:** Real-time Collaborative App | Project | 200 | Week 11 | 15% |
| **Major Project 3:** Analytics Platform | Project | 200 | Week 14 | 20% |

**Total Points:** 1100  
**Grading Scale:** A (93-100%), A- (90-92%), B+ (87-89%), B (83-86%), B- (80-82%), C+ (77-79%), C (70-76%), D (60-69%), F (<60%)

---

## Course Policies

### Attendance Policy
Regular attendance is essential for this hands-on course. More than 3 unexcused absences may result in course failure. Lab sessions are mandatory and cannot be made up without prior arrangement.

### Late Assignment Policy
- **Projects:** 10% penalty per day late (maximum 3 days, then 0 points)
- **Quizzes/Exams:** No makeup without documented excuse
- **Discussions:** Must be completed by due date (no late submissions)

### Collaboration Policy
- **Encouraged:** Peer programming during lab sessions, code reviews, discussing concepts
- **Prohibited:** Copying code, sharing project solutions, unauthorized collaboration on individual assessments

### Technology Requirements
- **Required Software:** Git, Node.js, Jest, Python, pytest, Docker, IDE of choice
- **Accounts Needed:** GitHub, cloud platform access (provided)
- **Hardware:** Laptop capable of running development tools and virtual machines

### Code Quality Standards
All submitted code must:
- Follow established style guidelines (ESLint, Prettier)
- Include comprehensive tests (minimum 80% coverage)

### Academic Integrity
This course emphasizes professional development practices. Any form of academic dishonesty will result in course failure. When in doubt about collaboration boundaries, ask the instructor.

### Accommodation Statement
Students with documented disabilities should contact the Office of Disability Services to arrange reasonable accommodations. Please discuss your needs with me as early as possible in the semester.

### Communication Policy

- Email responses within 24-48 hours on weekdays

This is an intensive, project-heavy course designed to prepare you for professional software development. Success requires consistent effort, active participation, and a commitment to learning industry-standard practices. The skills you develop here will directly transfer to your internships and full-time positions.

# Strategic Foresight Analytics: Building Decision Intelligence Systems
**Course Syllabus - Fall 2024**

---

## COURSE INFORMATION

**Course Code:** DATA 495  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Statistics (STAT 301), Database Management (DATA 301), Machine Learning (DATA 401)  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesday/Thursday 2:00-3:30 PM  

### Course Description
This capstone course transforms students into strategic forecasting consultants who design and implement comprehensive decision intelligence systems for real-world organizations. Students work directly with industry partners to tackle complex forecasting challenges across diverse sectors including retail demand planning, financial risk assessment, supply chain optimization, and market trend prediction. The course integrates advanced time series analysis, machine learning forecasting models, scenario planning methodologies, and uncertainty quantification techniques. Students develop end-to-end forecasting pipelines that incorporate multiple data sources, handle missing data and outliers, and provide actionable insights with confidence intervals. The capstone project requires teams to deliver a fully functional forecasting system complete with interactive dashboards, automated reporting, and business recommendations. Emphasis is placed on communicating forecast uncertainty to stakeholders, validating model performance over time, and adapting models to changing business conditions. By semester's end, students present their systems to industry partners and academic faculty, demonstrating both technical proficiency and strategic business acumen in transforming data into forward-looking intelligence.

### Learning Objectives
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Design and deploy enterprise-level forecasting systems** that integrate multiple algorithms and data sources for robust prediction accuracy
2. **Master advanced uncertainty quantification techniques** and communicate forecast reliability to non-technical stakeholders through compelling visualizations  
3. **Demonstrate consulting-level expertise** by delivering actionable strategic recommendations based on forecasting insights to real industry partners

---

# Digital Archaeology: Mining Hidden Patterns in Complex Datasets
**Course Code:** DATA 385

**Prerequisites:** Introduction to Statistics, Programming Fundamentals (Python preferred)  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays & Thursdays, 2:00-4:30 PM

## Course Description

This hands-on laboratory course transforms students into digital archaeologists who uncover hidden insights buried within complex, real-world datasets. Through intensive lab sessions, students excavate meaningful patterns from messy, unstructured data using advanced data mining techniques including association rule mining, clustering algorithms, anomaly detection, and sequential pattern discovery. The course emphasizes practical application through weekly laboratory exercises where students work with diverse datasets from social media streams, financial transactions, sensor networks, and customer behavior logs. Students learn to clean, preprocess, and systematically explore large datasets while developing proficiency in Python-based mining tools such as scikit-learn, Weka, and specialized libraries. Each lab session builds toward a capstone project where teams conduct an original data archaeology expedition on a dataset of their choice, presenting their discoveries through comprehensive reports and interactive visualizations. The laboratory environment simulates real-world data science scenarios, emphasizing reproducible research practices, ethical data handling, and effective communication of complex findings to non-technical stakeholders.

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• Master core data mining algorithms including clustering, classification, association rules, and outlier detection through hands-on implementation  
• Develop proficiency in excavating actionable insights from noisy, heterogeneous datasets using systematic exploration methodologies  
• Construct end-to-end data mining pipelines incorporating preprocessing, feature engineering, pattern discovery, and validation techniques  
• Demonstrate expertise in Python-based mining frameworks and visualization tools for presenting complex analytical findings  
• Apply ethical data mining practices and statistical validation methods to ensure reliable and responsible pattern discovery

# Temporal Pattern Mining and Predictive Analytics for Strategic Decision Making

**Course Code:** DATA 485  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** STAT 201 (Statistics), COMP 201 (Programming Fundamentals), DATA 301 (Introduction to Data Analytics)  
**Semester:** Fall 2024

## Instructor Information

## Course Description

This specialized course explores advanced forecasting methodologies through the lens of temporal pattern recognition and strategic business applications. Students will master cutting-edge techniques for extracting meaningful patterns from time-dependent data and translating these insights into actionable business forecasts. The curriculum emphasizes real-world applications across industries including supply chain optimization, financial market prediction, consumer behavior forecasting, and operational planning. Students will work with complex datasets featuring seasonal variations, trend analysis, and cyclical patterns while learning to handle data irregularities, missing values, and external shock events. The course integrates machine learning approaches with traditional econometric methods, covering ARIMA modeling, exponential smoothing, ensemble forecasting methods, and neural network-based prediction systems. Through hands-on projects using Python and R, students will build comprehensive forecasting pipelines that include data preprocessing, model selection, validation techniques, and uncertainty quantification. Special emphasis is placed on forecast accuracy assessment, business impact measurement, and communicating predictive insights to stakeholders. By semester's end, students will possess the technical expertise and strategic thinking necessary to drive data-informed decision-making in dynamic business environments.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master advanced time series decomposition techniques** and identify complex temporal patterns in multidimensional business data

3. **Develop expertise in forecast validation, uncertainty quantification**, and translating predictive analytics into actionable business recommendations

# Visual Storytelling with Complex Data: Advanced Techniques for Multi-Dimensional Analysis

**Course Code:** DATA 485  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** DATA 301 (Intermediate Data Analysis), STAT 342 (Statistical Computing), or equivalent  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays & Thursdays, 2:00-3:30 PM  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  

## Instructor Information

## Course Description
This advanced course explores the intersection of data science and visual communication, focusing on transforming complex, multi-dimensional datasets into compelling visual narratives. Students will master cutting-edge visualization techniques including interactive dashboards, animated time-series visualizations, network analysis graphics, and immersive data experiences using AR/VR technologies. The curriculum emphasizes advanced statistical visualization methods such as dimensionality reduction plots, uncertainty visualization, and comparative analysis frameworks. Students will work with real-world datasets from fields like genomics, social networks, financial markets, and climate science to create publication-quality visualizations and interactive web applications. The course combines theoretical foundations in human perception and cognitive load theory with hands-on practice using advanced tools like D3.js, Plotly, Tableau Public, and emerging visualization libraries. Projects culminate in developing comprehensive visual analysis portfolios that demonstrate the ability to extract actionable insights from complex data while effectively communicating findings to diverse stakeholders through sophisticated visual storytelling techniques.

## Learning Objectives
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Advanced Technical Implementation:** Design and implement advanced interactive visualizations using D3.js, Plotly, and specialized libraries for complex data types including networks, geospatial, and temporal data

2. **Cognitive Design Principles:** Apply cognitive science principles and perceptual theory to create visualizations that optimize human comprehension and minimize cognitive load in multi-dimensional data exploration

3. **Visual Narrative Construction:** Develop expertise in visual narrative construction, creating compelling data stories that guide audiences through complex analytical findings using advanced animation, layering, and interactive techniques

## Required Materials
- **Textbook:** "Storytelling with Data" by Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic

- **Hardware:** Laptop capable of running visualization software
- **Online Resources:** Course materials available on Learning Management System

### Week 4: Bivariate and Multivariate Relationships

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This hands-on course transforms students into business forecasters by combining statistical modeling with real-world market scenarios. Students work exclusively with live datasets from retail, finance, and e-commerce sectors to predict sales trends, customer behavior, and market movements. The curriculum emphasizes practical forecasting techniques including time series analysis, regression modeling, and machine learning algorithms specifically tailored for business prediction challenges. Each week features case studies from companies like Amazon, Netflix, and financial institutions, where students replicate actual forecasting problems and present solutions to simulated executive teams. Students will master industry-standard tools including Python's forecasting libraries, Tableau for visualization, and Excel's advanced analytics functions. The course culminates in a capstone project where teams partner with local businesses to solve genuine forecasting challenges, from inventory management to demand planning. # COURSE SYLLABUS

## TEMPORAL INTELLIGENCE: PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS AND STRATEGIC FORECASTING SYSTEMS
**Course Code:** DATA 485  
**Credits:** 4  
**Prerequisites:** Statistics (STAT 301), Programming for Data Analysis (DATA 301), Database Systems (CS 320)  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays/Thursdays 2:00-3:50 PM  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This advanced course integrates cutting-edge forecasting methodologies with real-world strategic decision-making frameworks. Students explore sophisticated time series analysis, machine learning-based prediction models, and hybrid forecasting systems used by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies. The curriculum emphasizes ensemble forecasting techniques, uncertainty quantification, and the integration of external data streams (economic indicators, social media sentiment, satellite imagery) into predictive models. 

Students work with streaming data architectures, implement dynamic model updating systems, and develop forecasting dashboards using cloud-based platforms. Special focus is placed on forecast accuracy evaluation, bias detection, and the communication of predictive insights to non-technical stakeholders. Case studies span multiple industries including supply chain optimization, financial risk assessment, energy demand planning, and epidemiological modeling. 

The course culminates in a capstone project where student teams partner with local organizations to solve real forecasting challenges, from conceptualization through deployment and monitoring. Graduates emerge with expertise in both the technical aspects of advanced forecasting and the business acumen to translate predictions into actionable strategic recommendations.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Design and implement ensemble forecasting systems** that combine multiple prediction algorithms to optimize accuracy across diverse temporal patterns
2. **Integrate heterogeneous data sources** (structured, unstructured, streaming) into unified forecasting frameworks and evaluate their predictive value
3. **Develop automated model selection and hyperparameter tuning pipelines** for time-varying forecasting environments
4. **Construct uncertainty quantification frameworks** that provide confidence intervals and risk assessments alongside point forecasts
5. **Create interactive forecasting dashboards and visualization tools** that effectively communicate predictive insights to business stakeholders

---

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

### Textbooks
- **Primary:** "Forecasting: Principles and Practice" (3rd ed.) by Hyndman & Athanasopoulos
- **Supplementary:** "Hands-On Machine Learning" (2nd ed.) by Aurélien Géron

### Software & Platforms
- Python 3.8+ with libraries: pandas, scikit-learn, statsmodels, plotly, streamlit
- R with forecast, tidyverse, and prophet packages
- Access to cloud platforms (AWS/Google Cloud credits provided)
- Jupyter Notebooks or RStudio

### Hardware
- Laptop capable of running data analysis software
- Minimum 8GB RAM recommended

---

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### Week 1: Foundations of Temporal Data Analysis
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization Fundamentals
- **Tuesday:** Course introduction, temporal data characteristics
- **Thursday:** Time series EDA techniques and pattern recognition
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Univariate analysis for temporal data - examining time-dependent variables through trend, seasonality, and cyclical pattern identification
  - Bivariate analysis - exploring relationships between temporal variables using lag correlation, cross-correlation, and time-aligned visualizations
- 
### Week 2: Time Series Decomposition and Preprocessing

# Pattern Discovery in Complex Data Ecosystems
**Course Code:** DATA 485  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** DATA 385 (Data Mining Fundamentals), STAT 301 (Statistical Methods), CS 210 (Data Structures)  
**Meeting Time:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM  

## Instructor Information

## Course Description
This advanced course explores sophisticated data mining techniques for extracting meaningful patterns from heterogeneous, high-dimensional datasets. Students will master cutting-edge algorithms for discovering hidden structures in complex data ecosystems including social networks, temporal sequences, and multi-modal datasets. The curriculum emphasizes practical implementation of advanced mining algorithms such as frequent pattern mining, graph-based clustering, anomaly detection in streaming data, and ensemble methods for pattern recognition. Students will work with real-world datasets from domains like bioinformatics, financial markets, and IoT sensor networks. The course integrates theoretical foundations with hands-on experience using specialized mining frameworks and distributed computing platforms. Advanced topics include association rule mining with constraints, sequential pattern discovery, subspace clustering, and interpretable machine learning for pattern explanation. Students will develop expertise in handling data quality challenges, scalability issues, and ethical considerations in pattern discovery. The capstone project requires students to design and implement a complete pattern discovery pipeline for a novel domain, demonstrating mastery of advanced mining techniques and their practical applications in solving complex real-world problems.

## Learning Objectives
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master Advanced Pattern Mining Algorithms:** Students will master advanced pattern mining algorithms including frequent itemset mining, sequential pattern discovery, and graph-based clustering techniques

2. **Apply Sophisticated Data Mining Methodologies:** Students will apply sophisticated data mining methodologies to extract actionable insights from complex, multi-dimensional datasets across diverse domains

3. **Develop Scalable Mining Solutions:** Students will develop expertise in implementing scalable mining solutions using distributed computing frameworks and evaluating pattern quality and significance

# Visual Storytelling Lab: From Raw Data to Compelling Narratives

**Course Code:** DATA 385  
**Credits:** 3 credit hours  
**Prerequisites:** Introduction to Statistics, Basic Programming (Python or R recommended)  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays & Thursdays, 2:00-3:50 PM  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  

---

## Course Description

This hands-on laboratory course transforms students into data storytellers who can craft compelling visual narratives from complex datasets. Students work exclusively in a collaborative lab environment, manipulating real-world datasets from journalism, healthcare, environmental science, and social media to create interactive dashboards, animated visualizations, and multimedia data stories. Each lab session focuses on a different storytelling challenge: revealing hidden patterns in messy data, designing visualizations for diverse audiences (executives, general public, policymakers), and building interactive experiences that guide viewers through data discoveries. Students master industry-standard tools including Tableau, D3.js, Python visualization libraries, and emerging AR/VR data presentation platforms. The course culminates in teams producing publication-ready data stories complete with interactive elements, following professional journalism and consulting standards. Emphasis is placed on ethical visualization practices, accessibility design, and understanding how visual choices influence audience interpretation. Students leave with a portfolio of data stories and the technical skills to turn any dataset into a persuasive, visually engaging narrative.

---

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Design and implement interactive data visualizations** that effectively communicate complex insights to diverse audiences
2. **Apply narrative storytelling techniques** to transform raw datasets into compelling, ethical visual stories using industry-standard tools
3. **Develop collaborative laboratory skills** for iterative design, user testing, and publication of professional-quality data narratives

---

## Required Materials

- **Software:** Python (Anaconda distribution), Tableau Public, GitHub account
- **Hardware:** Laptop capable of running visualization software
- **Textbook:** *Storytelling with Data* by Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic (recommended)
- **Online Resources:** Access to course datasets via Canvas

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundation Building
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Python
- **Topics:** 
  - Data profiling - systematic examination of dataset structure, completeness, and quality metrics
  - Univariate analysis - statistical and visual exploration of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
- **Lab Activity:** Introduction to Python visualization libraries (Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly)

### Week 2: Data Quality and Distribution Analysis
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization Fundamentals
- **Topics:**
  - Descriptive Statistics - measures of central tendency, variability, and distribution shape used to summarize dataset characteristics
  - Data Distribution Analysis - understanding normal, skewed, and multimodal distributions through histograms, box plots, and probability plots
- **Lab Activity:** Data quality assessment workshop with real-world messy datasets

### Week 3: Relationship Discovery
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization
- **Topics:**
  - Univariate analysis - examining individual variables through measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape including histograms, box plots, and summary statistics
  - Bivariate analysis - exploring relationships between two variables using scatter plots, correlation coefficients, cross-tabulations, and grouped summary statistics
- **Lab Activity:** Pattern discovery in journalism datasets

### Week 4: Anomaly Detection and Statistical Insights
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis: Uncovering Patterns and Anomalies
- **Topics:**
  - Univariate Analysis: Examining single variables through measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape to understand individual variable characteristics
  - Outlier Detection: Systematic identification of data points that deviate significantly from expected patterns using statistical methods like Z-scores and boxplot analysis
- **Lab Activity:** Healthcare data anomaly detection exercise

### Week 5: Visualization Principles and Design
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization Techniques

## Course Description
This specialized course explores advanced Bayesian statistical methods applied to real-world business decision-making scenarios. Students will master probabilistic reasoning, prior belief updating, and uncertainty quantification in data-driven environments. The curriculum emphasizes practical implementation of Bayesian inference techniques including Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, hierarchical modeling, and Bayesian A/B testing frameworks. Through industry case studies, students will analyze customer behavior patterns, optimize marketing campaigns, assess financial risks, and evaluate product performance using Bayesian paradigms. The course integrates modern computational tools including R/Stan and Python/PyMC for implementing complex Bayesian models. Students will develop expertise in communicating probabilistic results to stakeholders, constructing informative priors from domain knowledge, and designing robust decision frameworks under uncertainty. Emphasis is placed on comparing Bayesian approaches with frequentist methods, understanding when each paradigm is most appropriate, and interpreting credible intervals versus confidence intervals. By course completion, students will possess specialized skills in Bayesian data analysis that are increasingly valued in data science, consulting, and strategic analytics roles across various industries.

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master Bayesian Inference Fundamentals:** Students will master Bayesian inference techniques including prior specification, likelihood construction, and posterior interpretation for business analytics applications

# COURSE SYLLABUS
**Temporal Forecasting and Risk Prediction Analytics**

---

## COURSE INFORMATION

**Course Code:** DATA 485

**Class Schedule:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM  
**Laboratory:** Thursday 2:00-4:50 PM  
**Duration:** 16-week semester

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This advanced course focuses on building sophisticated predictive models for time-sensitive scenarios and risk assessment applications. Students will master cutting-edge techniques for forecasting temporal patterns, predicting market volatility, credit default risks, and operational failures across various industries. The curriculum emphasizes real-world implementation of ensemble methods, deep learning architectures for sequential data, and survival analysis techniques. Students will work with streaming data, handle concept drift, and develop early warning systems using advanced feature engineering and model validation strategies. Laboratory sessions involve hands-on experience with financial datasets, healthcare outcomes prediction, and supply chain forecasting. The course covers model interpretability, uncertainty quantification, and deployment considerations for high-stakes prediction systems. Students will complete a capstone project involving the development of a complete predictive analytics pipeline for a real client, incorporating model monitoring, automated retraining, and performance tracking. By course completion, students will possess industry-ready skills in temporal modeling, risk quantification, and the ability to architect robust predictive systems that perform reliably under changing conditions.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Master advanced time series forecasting techniques** including LSTM networks, ARIMA-GARCH models, and transformer architectures for temporal prediction
• **Develop expertise in risk modeling methodologies** including survival analysis, credit scoring models, and operational risk prediction systems  
• **Implement end-to-end predictive analytics pipelines** with automated model monitoring, drift detection, and dynamic retraining capabilities

---

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

**Textbooks:**
- Hyndman, R.J. & Athanasopoulos, G. *Forecasting: Principles and Practice* (3rd ed.)

**Software:**
- Python 3.8+ with Jupyter Lab
- Required libraries: pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, tensorflow, pytorch, statsmodels, plotly

- Time series components (trend, seasonality, cyclical, irregular)

- Autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation analysis

### **Week 3: Classical Forecasting MethodsTopics:**
- Moving averages and exponential smoothing
- Holt-Winters seasonal methods
- Model selection and parameter optimization

### **Week 4: ARIMA ModelsTopics:**
- Autoregressive (AR) and Moving Average (MA) models
- Box-Jenkins methodology for ARIMA modeling
- Model diagnostics and residual analysis

### **Week 5: Advanced Time Series ModelsTopics:**
- GARCH models for volatility forecasting
- Vector Autoregression (VAR) for multivariate series
- State space models and Kalman filtering

### **Week 6: Deep Learning for Sequential DataTopics:**
- Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) fundamentals
- Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks
- Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) and bidirectional architectures

### **Week 7: Transformer ArchitecturesTopics:**
- Attention mechanisms and self-attention
- Transformer models for temporal prediction
- Multi-head attention and positional encoding

### **Week 8: Risk Modeling FundamentalsTopics:**
- Types of risk (credit, market, operational)
- Probability of default models
- Loss given default and exposure at default

### **Week 9: Survival AnalysisTopics:**
- Survival functions and hazard rates
- Kaplan-Meier estimators
- Cox proportional hazards models

### **Week 10: Advanced Risk ModelsTopics:**
- Copula models for dependency modeling
- Value at Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall
- Stress testing and scenario analysis

### **Week 11: Ensemble MethodsTopics:**
- Random forests for time series
- Gradient boosting for temporal data
- Model stacking and blending strategies

### **Week 12: Streaming Data and Concept DriftTopics:**
- Online learning algorithms
- Concept drift detection methods
- Adaptive model updating strategies

### **Week 13: Model InterpretabilityTopics:**
- SHAP values for time series models
- Feature importance in temporal contexts
- Model explanation techniques

### **Week 14: Uncertainty QuantificationTopics:**
- Prediction intervals and confidence bounds
- Bayesian approaches to forecasting
- Monte Carlo methods for risk assessment

### **Week 15: Model Deployment and MonitoringTopics:**

# Project Blueprint Laboratory: Advanced Planning Simulation and Prototyping

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

Students work in teams to develop comprehensive project blueprints for real-world scenarios across multiple industries, utilizing cutting-edge planning software, physical modeling tools, and digital simulation platforms. The laboratory setting emphasizes iterative planning processes, where students construct, test, and refine project plans through controlled experiments and scenario-based challenges. Each week features different planning laboratories focusing on scope definition, resource allocation modeling, risk assessment simulations, and timeline optimization using both traditional and agile planning frameworks. **Readings:** Course packet Ch. 1-2
**Activity:** PMI-PMP Critical Path Method Terminology Mastery Challenge (60 minutes)

### Week 2: Quality Standards and Frameworks Overview
**Topics:** ISO 9001, TQM principles, quality management system components
**Readings:** ISO 9001 standards document (selected sections)
**Activity:** Project Management Knowledge Integration Framework (PMKIF) Recall Challenge (50 minutes)

### Week 3: Risk Management and Mitigation Strategies
**Module Concepts:**
- **Risk Register:** A comprehensive document that captures identified risks, their probability, impact, response strategies, and ownership assignments
- **Probability-Impact Matrix:** A qualitative assessment tool that plots risks on a grid to prioritize them based on likelihood of occurrence and potential consequences

**Readings:** Course packet Ch. 3
**Activity:** Critical Path Method (CPM) Formula Components Memory Challenge (45 minutes)

### Week 4: Six Sigma Methodology in Project Quality
**Topics:** DMAIC process, statistical process control, Six Sigma tools and techniques
**Readings:** Six Sigma case studies packet
**Activity:** Critical Path Method (CPM) Network Diagram Component Identification Challenge (40 minutes)

### Week 5: Lean Methodologies and Continuous Improvement
**Topics:** Waste elimination, value stream mapping, Kaizen events, Lean Six Sigma integration
**Readings:** Course packet Ch. 4-5
**Assessment:** Complex Project Crisis Management and Recovery Assessment (Quiz - 100 points)

**Topics:** Agile quality practices, DevOps quality gates, automated testing, code review processes

# Financial Dynamics and Resource Allocation Theory in Complex Projects
**Course Code:** PM 485  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Project Management Fundamentals (PM 201), Managerial Economics (ECON 340)  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This advanced theoretical course examines the intricate relationship between financial planning, resource allocation, and project success through multiple economic and organizational lenses. Students explore cutting-edge budgeting frameworks including earned value management, Monte Carlo cost simulation, and dynamic resource optimization models. The curriculum emphasizes theoretical foundations of cost estimation methodologies, risk-adjusted budget modeling, and stakeholder financial decision-making processes. Through rigorous analysis of budget variance theories, students investigate how financial constraints shape project scope, timeline, and quality outcomes. The course integrates behavioral economics principles to understand budget bias, escalation commitment, and resource allocation psychology in project environments. Students examine case studies of budget failures and successes across industries, analyzing root causes through theoretical frameworks rather than practical application. Advanced topics include portfolio-level budget optimization, cross-project resource sharing models, and the impact of organizational financial culture on project budgeting practices. This theoretical foundation prepares students to understand the deeper economic and psychological forces that drive project financial decision-making, enabling them to critically evaluate and improve budgeting practices in future professional roles.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master advanced theoretical frameworks** for project cost estimation, budget variance analysis, and resource allocation optimization models
2. **Apply behavioral economics and organizational psychology theories** to analyze financial decision-making biases and budget-related project failures
3. **Develop expertise in evaluating complex budgeting methodologies** including Monte Carlo simulation, earned value management, and dynamic resource optimization theories

# Zero-Defect Project Delivery: Advanced Quality Assurance and Risk Mitigation in Complex Project Environments

**Course Code:** PM 4850  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** PM 3000 (Project Management Fundamentals), STAT 2500 (Business Statistics)  
**Semester:** Spring 2024

## Instructor Information

## Course Description
This intensive 15-week course immerses students in the critical discipline of quality assurance within high-stakes project management environments. Students engage in real-world project simulations where quality failures have cascading consequences, learning to implement rigorous QA frameworks, statistical process control, and proactive defect prevention strategies. The course emphasizes hands-on application of Six Sigma principles, ISO 9001 quality management systems, and advanced testing methodologies across diverse project types including software development, construction, pharmaceutical, and aerospace projects. Through intensive case study analysis of notable project failures (Challenger disaster, Denver Airport baggage system, Healthcare.gov launch), students develop expertise in quality planning, assurance auditing, control charting, and corrective action protocols. The curriculum integrates cutting-edge quality tools including failure mode analysis, quality function deployment, and automated testing frameworks. Students work in rotating project teams under compressed timelines, experiencing firsthand how quality assurance decisions impact project success, stakeholder satisfaction, and organizational reputation. By course completion, students possess advanced competencies in quality metrics development, vendor quality management, regulatory compliance frameworks, and the leadership skills necessary to champion quality-first project cultures in demanding professional environments.

## Learning Objectives
Upon successful completion of this course, students will:

• Master advanced quality assurance frameworks including Six Sigma, Lean, and ISO 9001 standards for complex project environments  
• Apply statistical process control methods and predictive quality analytics to prevent defects before they impact project deliverables  
• Develop expertise in quality audit protocols, vendor quality management, and regulatory compliance across multiple industry sectors  
• Demonstrate proficiency in quality planning, risk-based testing strategies, and corrective action implementation under compressed project timelines  
• Synthesize quality management principles with stakeholder communication and change management to build sustainable quality cultures

This comprehensive survey course examines how successful project leaders anticipate, assess, and mitigate risks across diverse industries and project types. course_info.description: This experiential course transforms students into coaching-minded leaders who develop talent through purposeful dialogue and empowerment strategies. # THE LEADER AS COACH: DEVELOPING OTHERS THROUGH STRATEGIC CONVERSATIONS

**Course Code:** LDRS 3450  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** LDRS 2100 (Introduction to Leadership) or equivalent  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays & Thursdays, 2:00-3:15 PM  
**Classroom:** Leadership Lab 205  

---

## INSTRUCTOR INFORMATION

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION
This experiential course transforms students into coaching-minded leaders who develop talent through purposeful dialogue and empowerment strategies. Students engage in real-world coaching simulations, practice structured feedback conversations, and master the art of asking powerful questions that unlock potential in others. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on application through peer coaching partnerships, case study analysis of coaching failures and successes, and development of personalized coaching frameworks. Students will conduct actual coaching sessions with volunteer participants, receive video feedback on their coaching conversations, and build a toolkit of evidence-based coaching interventions. The course challenges traditional command-and-control leadership models by focusing on collaborative leadership approaches that prioritize employee development, psychological safety, and performance enhancement through supportive guidance rather than directive management. By semester's end, students will possess measurable coaching competencies and a portfolio of successful coaching interventions, preparing them to lead through influence, curiosity, and developmental mindset rather than positional authority.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Demonstrate proficiency in conducting structured coaching conversations** using evidence-based questioning techniques and active listening skills
2. **Design and implement personalized development plans** for team members through systematic coaching interventions and feedback mechanisms
3. **Apply coaching methodologies** to resolve workplace conflicts, enhance team performance, and facilitate organizational change initiatives

---

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### **Week 1: Introduction to Coaching Leadership**
- Course overview and coaching philosophy
- Self-assessment: Current leadership and coaching competencies
- Introduction to peer coaching partnerships

### **Week 2: Emotional Intelligence FoundationsModule:** *Emotional Intelligence in Leadership: Building Self-Awareness and Social Skills*
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Self-Awareness: Recognizing and understanding one's own emotions, strengths, weaknesses, and values in real-time
  - Self-Management: Managing disruptive emotions and impulses while maintaining flexibility and optimism
- **Activity:** Emotional Intelligence Self-Assessment and Reflection (60 minutes)

### **Week 3: Emotional Intelligence in PracticeModule:** *Emotional Intelligence in Leadership: Building Self-Awareness and Social Skills*
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Self-Awareness: Recognizing emotions, strengths, weaknesses, and values in real-time
  - Social Awareness: Reading others' emotions accurately, understanding organizational dynamics, and demonstrating empathy
- **Activity:** Peer Coaching Practice: Emotional Intelligence Application (90 minutes)

### **Week 4: Emotional Contagion and Leadership ImpactModule:** *Emotional Intelligence in Leadership: Building Self-Awareness and Social Skills*
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Self-Awareness: Understanding personal emotions and their impact on leadership effectiveness
  - Emotional Contagion: How emotions spread from leader to team members, influencing group mood and performance
- **Activity:** Video Analysis of Leadership Emotional Impact (75 minutes)

### **Week 5: Transformational Leadership as CoachingModule:** *Transformational Leadership: Inspiring Vision and Driving Change*
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Idealized Influence: Serving as role models, earning trust through ethical behavior and integrity
  - Inspirational Motivation: Articulating compelling visions and inspiring enthusiasm for shared goals
- **Activity:** Deconstructing Transformational Leadership Through Crisis Case Study Analysis (160 minutes)

### **Week 6: Advanced Transformational CoachingModule:** *Transformational Leadership: Inspiring Vision and Change*
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Idealized Influence: Demonstrating high ethical standards and earning trust through consistent behavior
  - Inspirational Motivation: Articulating compelling future visions that energize and motivate others
- **Activity:** Vision Coaching Practice Sessions (120 minutes)

### **Week 7: Situational Coaching ModelModule:** *Situational Leadership: Adapting Your Style to Context and People*
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Situational Leadership Model: Varying directive and supportive behaviors based on follower readiness
  - Development Level: Combination of competence and commitment for specific tasks or goals
- **Activity:** Situational Coaching Simulations (90 minutes)

### **Week 8: Advanced Situational Coaching ApplicationsModule:** *Situational Leadership: Adapting Your Style to Team Needs*
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Development Level (D1-D4): Competence and commitment combinations from enthusiastic beginner to self-reliant achiever
  - Leadership Styles (S1-S4): Directing, Coaching, Supporting, and Delegating approaches
- **Activity:** Multi-Scenario Coaching Practice (105 minutes)

### **Week 9: MIDTERM WEEK - Assessment & Reflection**
- **Assessment:** Strategic Leadership Crisis Simulation and Analysis (Quiz - 100 points)
- Peer coaching partnership evaluations
- Mid-course coaching competency assessment

### **Week 10: Performance-Driven Situational CoachingModule:** *Situational Leadership: Adapting Your Style to Drive Team Performance*
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Development Level (D1-D4): Competence and commitment determining follower readiness
  - Leadership Styles (S1-S4): Four distinct approaches varying in directive and supportive behaviors
- **Activity:** Performance Coaching Case Studies (100 minutes)

### **Week 11: Adaptive Leadership CoachingModule:** *Adaptive Leadership: Navigating Complex Challenges and Uncertainty*
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Technical vs. Adaptive Challenges: Known solutions vs. requiring new learning and innovative approaches
  - The Balcony and Dance Floor: Moving between direct engagement and strategic observation
- **Activity:** Analyzing Leadership Paradoxes Through Multi-Stakeholder Impact Mapping (125 minutes)

### **Week 12: Creating Holding EnvironmentsModule:** *Adaptive Leadership: Navigating Complex Challenges and Change*
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Technical vs. Adaptive Challenges: Expert solutions vs. stakeholder learning and behavioral change
  - Holding Environment: Psychological space containing stress while maintaining safety for productive dialogue
- **Activity:** Deconstructing Leadership Paradoxes: Analyzing Real-World Executive Decision-Making Tensions (125 minutes)

### **Week 13: Advanced Coaching Interventions**
- Difficult conversation coaching techniques
- Conflict resolution through coaching approaches
- Coaching for organizational change
- **Activity:** Crisis Communication Coaching Simulations (95 minutes)

### **Week 14: Real-World Coaching Practice**
- Students conduct coaching sessions with volunteer participants
- Video feedback and analysis sessions
- Peer coaching supervision and feedback
- **Activity:** Live Coaching Laboratory (180 minutes)

### **Week 15: Integration and Portfolio Development**
- Coaching competency demonstrations
- Portfolio completion and peer reviews
- Course reflection and future development planning

### **Week 16: FINALS WEEK**
- **Final Assessment:** Transformational Leadership Portfolio: Real-World Impact Documentation (Portfolio - 100 points)
- Final coaching demonstrations
- Course celebration and networking

# The Silent Stage: Mastering Nonverbal Communication in High-Stakes Leadership
**Course Code:** LEAD 4XX | **Credits:** 3 | **Semester:** Fall/Spring 20XX  
**Prerequisites:** Introduction to Leadership Principles or equivalent

## INSTRUCTOR INFORMATION

## COURSE DESCRIPTION
This intensive semester-long course explores the critical role of nonverbal communication in leadership effectiveness across crisis situations, multicultural teams, and high-pressure environments. Students engage in immersive simulation exercises, real-time video analysis, and field observations to decode and master the subtle art of body language, spatial dynamics, vocal tonality, and cultural nonverbal cues that often determine leadership success or failure. Through partnership with local organizations, students will conduct live leadership assessments and provide nonverbal communication coaching to actual leaders. The course combines neuroscience research on nonverbal processing with practical application through weekly leadership scenarios including boardroom negotiations, crisis management briefings, and cross-cultural team dynamics. Students will develop a personal nonverbal leadership signature while learning to read and respond to the unspoken communication of followers, peers, and stakeholders. This intensive format requires significant field work, peer coaching sessions, and real-world application projects that push students beyond traditional classroom learning into authentic leadership communication challenges.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Decode and strategically utilize nonverbal communication patterns** to enhance leadership credibility and influence in diverse organizational contexts
2. **Apply intensive observation and coaching techniques** to improve their own and others' nonverbal leadership presence through systematic feedback and analysis
3. **Develop cultural competency in nonverbal communication** across different organizational and international contexts, adapting their leadership style accordingly

# Leading Through Conversation: The Art of Influential Communication
**Course Code:** LEAD 3350  
**Credits:** 3  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  
**Class Time:** Tuesday/Thursday 2:00-3:20 PM  

---

## Course Description

This course explores how exceptional leaders use strategic conversation to inspire, persuade, and transform organizations. Students will examine the communication patterns of successful leaders across various contexts, from startup CEOs to community organizers, discovering how intentional dialogue creates lasting change. Through interactive simulations, students practice essential conversational skills including active listening, storytelling for impact, difficult conversation navigation, and multicultural communication competency. The course emphasizes practical application through role-playing exercises, peer coaching sessions, and real-world case study analysis. Students learn to recognize their own communication strengths and blind spots while developing authentic leadership voices. Key topics include nonverbal communication mastery, digital communication leadership, crisis communication strategies, and building psychological safety through inclusive dialogue. Unlike traditional leadership courses focusing on theory, this class centers on the daily communication choices that distinguish effective leaders. Students will create personal communication action plans and practice adapting their style to diverse audiences and situations. By semester's end, participants will possess concrete tools for leading meaningful conversations that drive engagement, build trust, and catalyze positive change in any organizational or community setting.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master foundational conversational leadership techniques** including active listening, empathetic responding, and strategic questioning to build trust and influence
2. **Apply storytelling frameworks and persuasive communication models** to craft compelling messages that inspire action and drive organizational change
3. **Develop cultural competency in communication** by practicing inclusive dialogue techniques and adapting their leadership style to diverse audiences and contexts

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundation of Conversational Leadership
**Topics:** Course introduction, communication as leadership foundation
**Readings:** Course packet Ch. 1-2
**Activities:** Communication style self-assessment, introductory dialogue exercises

### Week 2: Self-Awareness in Communication Leadership
**Module:** Emotional Intelligence in Leadership: Building Self-Awareness and Social Skills
- Self-Awareness: The ability to recognize and understand one's own emotions, strengths, weaknesses, and values, and their impact on others
- Social Awareness: The capacity to accurately read and understand others' emotions, organizational dynamics, and social networks

**Activity:** Personal communication audit and peer feedback session

### Week 3: Active Listening and Empathetic Leadership
**Module:** Emotional Intelligence in Leadership: Building Self-Awareness and Empathy
- Self-Awareness: The ability to recognize and understand your own emotions, strengths, weaknesses, and values, and their impact on others
- Self-Regulation: The capacity to manage disruptive emotions and impulses, maintaining composure and thinking before acting

**Activity:** Advanced listening techniques workshop and practice sessions

### Week 4: Strategic Questioning and Dialogue Facilitation
**Topics:** Question frameworks, facilitating meaningful conversations
**Readings:** Course packet Ch. 5-6
**Assessment:** Strategic Leadership Crisis Management Assessment (Quiz) - 100 points

### Week 5: Adaptive Communication in Complex Situations
**Module:** Adaptive Leadership: Navigating Complex Challenges and Change
- Technical vs. Adaptive Challenges: Technical problems have known solutions and clear authority structures, while adaptive challenges require learning, experimentation, and changes in values or behaviors
- The Balcony and Dance Floor: The ability to move between observing systems from a detached perspective (balcony) and engaging directly in the action (dance floor) to diagnose and intervene effectively

**Activity:** Deconstructing Adaptive Leadership Through Crisis Decision Analysis (150 minutes - extended class)

### Week 6: Situational Communication Leadership
**Module:** Situational Leadership: Adapting Your Style to Context and Team Needs
- Development Level (D1-D4): The combination of competence (knowledge, skills, experience) and commitment (motivation, confidence) that determines follower readiness
- Leadership Styles (S1-S4): Four distinct approaches ranging from Directing (high directive, low supportive) to Delegating (low directive, low supportive)

### Week 7: Storytelling for Leadership Impact
**Topics:** Narrative frameworks, compelling story structure, storytelling in organizational contexts
**Readings:** Course packet Ch. 9-10
**Activity:** Story development workshop and peer coaching

### Week 8: Persuasive Communication and Influence
**Topics:** Influence models, ethical persuasion, building compelling arguments
**Activity:** Deconstructing Leadership Paradoxes: Multi-Framework Analysis of Complex Scenarios (100 minutes)
**Assessment:** Strategic Leadership Crisis Simulation: Multi-Stakeholder Decision Making (Discussion) - 100 points

### Week 9: SPRING BREAK - No Classes

- Technical vs. Adaptive Challenges: Technical problems have known solutions and can be solved by experts; adaptive challenges require new learning, changed behaviors, and shifts in values or beliefs

### Week 13: Digital Communication Leadership

# COURSE SYLLABUS

## Course Description

This advanced theoretical course examines the psychological, sociological, and organizational foundations of how teams transcend individual capabilities to achieve collective intelligence. Students explore cutting-edge theories including distributed cognition, social identity theory, and systems thinking to understand team synergy mechanisms. The course analyzes team formation stages, role differentiation, communication networks, and decision-making processes through multiple theoretical lenses including Tuckman's model, Belbin's team roles, and complexity leadership theory. Emphasis is placed on understanding how diverse teams leverage cognitive diversity, manage conflict constructively, and develop shared mental models. Students critically examine case studies of high-performing teams across industries—from surgical teams to innovation labs—applying theoretical frameworks to analyze success factors. The curriculum integrates neuroscience research on group dynamics, social psychology theories on trust and psychological safety, and organizational behavior models of team effectiveness. Through theoretical analysis rather than hands-on activities, students develop sophisticated understanding of the scientific principles underlying exceptional team performance, preparing them to design and lead teams that harness collective intelligence for complex problem-solving and innovation.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Analyze** complex team dynamics using advanced theoretical frameworks from psychology, sociology, and organizational science
2. **Evaluate** how collective intelligence emerges through systematic application of team development theories and cognitive diversity principles  
3. **Synthesize** multiple theoretical perspectives to design evidence-based strategies for optimizing team performance and collaborative problem-solving

## Required Materials

- **Access to:** Academic databases for research projects

**Readings:** Heifetz & Laurie (2001) "The Work of Leadership"

**Readings:** Heifetz et al. (2009) "The Practice of Adaptive Leadership"

**Readings:** Boin & Hart (2003) "Public Leadership in Times of Crisis"

### Week 7: Complex Adaptive Systems
**Module:** Adaptive Leadership: Navigating Complex Challenges and Change  
**Key Concepts:**

- Holding Environment: Creating psychological safety for adaptive work

**Readings:** Uhl-Bien & Marion (2009) "Complexity Leadership in Bureaucratic Forms"

### Week 8: Advanced Emotional Intelligence Applications
**Module:** Emotional Intelligence in Leadership: Managing Self and Others  
**Key Concepts:**
- Self-Awareness: Real-time recognition of emotions and values

**Activity:** Deconstructing Crisis Leadership: Analyzing Decision-Making Frameworks (140 minutes)
